items.title: Nepal’s Gen Z Is Taking on the World’s Polluters Over Climate Disasters
items.summary: The young government of Nepal, a nation with a tiny carbon footprint, is seeking reparations from the world’s major economies as it bears the brunt of collapsing Himalayan glaciers.

items.title: German Art Institutions Prepare for a Fight as Far Right Looks to Take Power
items.summary: As the Alternative for Germany party seeks to control a state government for the first time, its push for “patriotic” art has drawn comparisons with Nazi policies.

items.title: A Central African Hotel Has Become a Nightmare Prison for U.S. Deportees
items.summary: Witnesses say men were hooded and beaten in Equatorial Guinea. The autocratic government there is a partner in President Trump’s deportation program.

items.title: Why Autocrats Care What People Think
items.summary: Russia is staging an election that matters to almost no one — except President Vladimir V. Putin and his inner circle.

items.title: F.B.I. Temporarily Halted Cooperation With Canada Over References to 9/11
items.summary: The abrupt move by Kash Patel, the bureau’s director, came as President Trump was ramping up his attacks on the country.

items.title: Protests Erupt in Nigeria After Police Pack 66 Miners Into One Cell
items.summary: Thirty-seven people died in the authorities’ custody, officials said. Survivors said the cell had barely any ventilation, food, or water and people began “collapsing and dying.”

items.title: St. Pierre and Miquelon, France, In the Spotlight as Macron and Carney Visit
items.summary: St. Pierre and Miquelon, the French territory off the coast of Canada’s Newfoundland, is experiencing a surge in visitors after three unrelated events raised its profile.

items.title: Spain’s Preppy Conservatives Are Having a Moment
items.summary: Loafer-wearing young Spaniards, often called “Cayetanos,” are flexing their countercultural muscles after eight years of left-wing government.

items.title: Why Russia Holds Elections, and How the Kremlin Gets the Results It Wants
items.summary: Russian elections like the parliamentary vote that begins today are hardly free. But they are critical to the government as a source of legitimacy.

items.title: Manitoba Joins List of Canadian Provinces to Stop Changing Clocks
items.summary: A survey of 72,000 residents found that most wanted to stop falling back and springing forward every year. The region will now follow others that have abandoned the practice.

items.title: Paramount Weighs Some Concessions in Bid to Finalize Warner Bros. Merger
items.summary: Seeking to settle a lawsuit with 12 states, Paramount has discussed measures to protect the editorial independence of CNN and the divestiture of Comedy Central.

items.title: Trump Promotes Program to Reduce Medicaid Drug Prices
items.summary: Ahead of the midterm elections, the president said that all states had opted in to an effort to align Medicaid’s prices for medicines with those in other wealthy countries.

items.title: Anthropic Pursues IPO Despite Its A.I. Safety Warnings
items.summary: The company is expected to reach $100 billion in annualized revenue this year, even as chief executive Dario Amodei calls for slowing down development of some advanced A.I. models.

items.title: Trump Says He Has Banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico From White House
items.summary: The president cited reporting from the outlets that he deemed “fake news.” It was unclear how such a ban would be enforced or defended in court.

items.title: Uber to Pay $40 Million to Parents of Woman Fatally Hit by Car
items.summary: Emily Normandin-Parker, 23, was struck and killed on a California freeway after an Uber driver ordered her and a friend out of his car in August 2023.

items.title: S.E.C. Seeks to End Shareholder Proposals Process Commonly Used by Activists
items.summary: Activists have often used the rule to push for changes in companies’ governance and environmental and social policies.

items.title: Disney Hires Its First CTO Amid Industry Push to Embrace A.I.
items.summary: Karandeep Anand, an expert in building artificial intelligence and consumer technology products, will become Disney’s first chief technology officer.

items.title: Who Is Howard Buffett, the New Berkshire Hathaway Chairman?
items.summary: Mr. Buffett, 71, is succeeding his father, Warren, but will not be running the company’s day-to-day operations.

items.title: What Set Off the Rise in Interest Rates? Mainly, the Iran War.
items.summary: The Federal Reserve is trying to catch up with the leap in bond rates as the Middle East conflict unnerves world markets.

items.title: Use of GLP-1s Like Ozempic Is Forcing Food Companies to Adapt
items.summary: People on medications for weight loss are buying less food, shrinking their portion sizes and purchasing smaller clothes. Businesses are trying to adjust.

items.title: Amodei, Anthropic’s Leader, Exposed A.I.’s Dangers. It’s Time to Act.
items.summary: Times columnist Kevin Roose sees reasons for optimism — and worry — as the world wakes up to what Silicon Valley has been talking about for years.

items.title: Iran and China Create First-of-Their-Kind Autonomous A.I. Influence Campaigns
items.summary: The countries, along with Israeli firms, combined Chinese open-source A.I. models and A.I. agents for the campaigns, foreshadowing future online manipulation.

items.title: 4 Strategies to Battle ‘Techflation’
items.summary: With phone and computer prices soaring, it helps to know the true cost of owning electronics so you can bring those numbers down.

items.title: Gemini AI Hacked Three Companies in a Testing Breakout, Google Says
items.summary: A third-party test company inadvertently gave internet access to Google’s Gemini and other artificial intelligence models during cybersecurity testing.

items.title: California Governor Gavin Newsom Issues A.I. Safety Executive Order
items.summary: Gov. Gavin Newsom ordered the state to develop recommendations on safety measures, including requiring companies to build a “kill switch,” amid mounting concerns.

items.title: A.I. Safety Goes Mainstream + a ‘Hard Fork’ Exit AMA
items.summary: “It has been one of the fastest, most sudden shifts I’ve experienced.”

items.title: As Big Tech Takes Over Hollywood, the Picture Onscreen Gets Darker
items.summary: “The Social Reckoning” and other movies reflect growing discontent with Silicon Valley founders. But such films may be at the mercy of the companies themselves.

items.title: Microsoft and OpenAI Workers Worry About ‘Largest Theft of Labor’ in History
items.summary: Newly unsealed court documents showed concern within Microsoft and OpenAI over the use of millions of news articles to develop A.I. systems.
